title: Talking About Money and Banking
summary: Learn useful words for managing your money at the bank. You will practice how to talk about saving, spending, and using accounts.

sections.p: When you have money, you need a safe place to put it. A bank is a business that keeps your money safe. You can open a bank account, which is your personal space at the bank. Every month, you might get a bank statement. This is a piece of paper or a digital file that shows all your money coming in and going out.

ex.en: I need to open a new bank account today.
ex.mean: I want to start a new relationship with a bank to keep my money.

ex.en: Please check your bank statement to see where your money went.
ex.mean: Look at the list of your recent money actions.

sections.h: Putting Money In and Taking Money Out
sections.p: When you work, your employer gives you money. You can deposit this money into your account, which means you put it in. When you need cash to buy food or clothes, you can withdraw money, which means you take it out of your account using an ATM or by talking to a cashier.

ex.en: I will deposit my paycheck into my savings account.
ex.mean: I am going to put the money I earned into the bank.

ex.en: I need to withdraw some cash for the bus.
ex.mean: I must take physical money out of the bank machine.

sections.p: It is always a good idea to put some money aside for later. This is called saving money. You can put extra money into a savings account. Sometimes, the bank gives you a little extra money as a reward for keeping your money there. This extra money is called interest.

ex.en: I am trying to save money for a nice holiday.
ex.mean: I am keeping my money instead of spending it right now.

ex.en: This account gives me a good rate of interest.
ex.mean: The bank pays me a little extra money for using their account.

tip: Try to label the things around you with English banking words, like writing 'ATM' on a picture of a cash machine to remember it easily.
